reproduction: Create one valid sealed offer for synthetic company/admin and obtain its GET CSRF value
Use two independent service-role PostgreSQL sessions, BEGIN both transactions, and call auth_rate_hit for the same picker nonce hash with max=1
Allow both function calls to return before either transaction commits. Each sees only its own inserted row and returns true
The actual-route test applies the identical legal timing to both POST RPC transactions, commits them and returns their real results
Both actual POSTs pass the single-use gate, reach the recording Xero refresh/store flow, and return 200. A later sequential replay correctly returns 410
findings.recommended_fix: Replace the picker use of the approximate rate limiter with an atomic service-only consumed-nonce claim scoped to company/admin/purpose, using a unique record or a correctly serialized database operation. Preserve expiry, recent MFA, CSRF, company binding, OFF and held-document gates. Opus owns any approved SQL change; do not rewrite protected historical migration 011 or introduce production SQL in this test PR.
findings.severity_scope: Strict single-use guarantee fails under concurrency. Existing company/tenant store constraints still protect their own invariants; no transfers or held releases were observed.
